learn.hook: 4² − 3² = 7, 5² − 4² = 9, 6² − 5² = 11... odd numbers keep popping out. Why? Draw squares and see!
points: Number patterns hint at identities: (n + 1)² − n² is always 2n + 1, the odd number n + (n + 1).
(a + b)²: a square of side a + b splits into an a × a square, a b × b square and two a × b rectangles, so it equals a² + 2ab + b².
(a − b)²: from the a × a square cut off two a × b strips (they overlap in a b × b square, which gets removed twice), so add b² back: a² − 2ab + b².
(a + b)(a − b): cut a b × b square from an a × a square and rearrange the L-shape into an (a + b) × (a − b) rectangle, so it equals a² − b².
(x + a)(x + b): a rectangle of sides x + a and x + b splits into x², ax, bx and ab, so it equals x² + (a + b)x + ab.

example.q: A square of side (x + 3) is split into pieces. List their areas and the total.

learn.reallife: Tilers covering a square floor with a border find the tile count using exactly these area splits.

games.title: Area model check
items: A square of side a + b contains two a × b rectangles.
The area of an (x + 4) × (x + 1) rectangle is x² + 4x + 4.
In the (a − b)² model, the b × b corner is removed twice, so b² is added back.

quiz.q: Using the pattern (n + 1)² − n² = 2n + 1, what is 51² − 50²?
quiz.mistake: Thinks consecutive squares differ by 1

quiz.q: A square of side (a + b) is cut into 4 pieces. Which list gives their areas?
quiz.explain: A side split into a and b gives an a × a square, a b × b square and two a × b rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the two rectangles

quiz.q: In the area model of (a − b)² with a = 12 cm and b = 3 cm, what is the area of the square that is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 2ab but forgets to add b² back

quiz.q: From a 10 × 10 square, a 4 × 4 corner is cut away. The L-shape is rearranged into a rectangle. What are its sides?
quiz.explain: The L-shape rearranges into (a + b) × (a − b) = 14 × 6 = 84 = 100 − 16.
quiz.mistake: Uses a and b as the sides

quiz.q: What is the area of the L-shape left when a 4 × 4 square is cut from a 10 × 10 square?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the side lengths and squares

quiz.q: A rectangle has sides (x + 3) and (x + 5). What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first terms and the last terms

quiz.q: In the area model of (x + a)(x + b), which piece gives the constant term ab?
quiz.explain: The rectangle made from the parts a and b has area ab.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the constant comes from the big square

quiz.q: Which identity does the pattern 3² − 2² = 5, 4² − 3² = 7, 5² − 4² = 9 come from?
quiz.explain: The difference of consecutive squares is always the next odd number 2n + 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 2n part of the expansion

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "Why is (a + b)² not just a² + b²? Show me with a picture!"
teach.praise: Lovely! The big square has two extra a × b rectangles, so 2ab!
teach.nudge: Draw a square of side a + b. What pieces do you see apart from a² and b²?

learn.hook: Can you find 103 × 103 in your head in five seconds? With the right identity, you can!
points: An identity is an equality that is true for every value of the variables, unlike an equation such as x + 2 = 5, which is true for only one value.
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². Picture a square of side a + b split into an a × a square, a b × b square and two a × b rectangles.
(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
(x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab.

steps: 103 = 100 + 3, so use (a + b)² with a = 100, b = 3

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers who multiply mentally often use these tricks: 49 × 51 = 50² − 1² = 2499.

games.title: Match each product with its expansion

quiz.q: Expand (x + 7)².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the middle term 2ab and writes x² + 49

quiz.q: Use (a − b)² to find 98².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the middle term (getting 9804) or drops the + b² (getting 9600)

quiz.q: Find 47 × 53 using an identity.
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Expand (3a − 2b)².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the middle term, writing 6ab

quiz.q: Expand (x + 4)(x − 9).
quiz.explain: Use (x + a)(x + b) with a = 4, b = −9: a + b = −5 and ab = −36.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of the middle term wrong

quiz.q: If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, find a² + b².
quiz.explain: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, so a² + b² = 100 − 42 = 58. Check with a = 3, b = 7: 9 + 49 = 58.
quiz.mistake: Takes a² + b² = (a + b)², forgetting the 2ab

quiz.q: Which of these is an identity (true for every value of x)?
quiz.explain: (x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1 holds for every x. The others are true only for some values (or are false in general).
quiz.mistake: Confuses an equation that is true for one value with an identity

quiz.q: Find 1002² − 998².
quiz.mistake: Uses only a − b and forgets to multiply by a + b

teach.ask: Gappu groans: "Why isn't (a + b)² just a² + b²? That looks so much simpler!"
teach.praise: Of course! The big square also has two a × b rectangles, so (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² for every value. I won't forget 2ab now!
teach.nudge: If you draw a square of side a + b, what pieces do you see besides a² and b²?

learn.hook: Expanding is like opening a gift box; factorising is packing it back. Identities show you how the box was folded!
points: To factorise means to write an expression as a product of simpler expressions.
Always take out a common factor first: 3x² − 75 = 3(x² − 25).
Look for patterns: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b); a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)²; a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)².
For x² + px + q, find two numbers with sum p and product q: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4).
a³ + b³ and a³ − b³ have their own factor forms. Always check by expanding your answer.

steps: Middle term: 2 × 2x × 3 = 12x, with a minus sign
So it matches a² − 2ab + b² with a = 2x, b = 3

learn.reallife: If a rectangular rangoli has area x² + 9x + 20, factorising tells you possible side lengths: (x + 4) and (x + 5).

games.title: Match each expression with its factors
Factorise 3x² − 75
items: Spot a difference of squares: x² − 5²

quiz.q: Factorise 9y² − 16.
quiz.mistake: Writes a difference of squares as a perfect square

quiz.q: Factorise x² + 8x + 16.
quiz.mistake: Finds numbers with product 16 but ignores the sum 8

quiz.q: Factorise x² − 7x + 12.
quiz.explain: We need two numbers with sum −7 and product 12: −3 and −4.
quiz.mistake: Uses + signs even though the middle term is negative

quiz.q: Factorise 2x² − 18 completely.
quiz.explain: Take out 2 to get 2(x² − 9), then x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
quiz.mistake: Stops after taking out the common factor

quiz.q: Use factorisation to find 87² − 13².
quiz.mistake: Computes (87 − 13)² = 5476 instead

quiz.q: Factorise x² + x − 20.
quiz.explain: Two numbers with product −20 and sum +1 are 5 and −4.
quiz.mistake: Puts the signs the wrong way round, giving a sum of −1

quiz.q: Factorise 27a³ − 8.
quiz.mistake: Uses a minus sign in the second bracket, mixing it up with a³ + b³

quiz.q: A rectangular rangoli has area x² + 9x + 20 square units. One side is (x + 4). What is the other side?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 4 from 20 instead of dividing, or uses the coefficient 9

teach.ask: Gappu stares at x² − 49: "How do I break this into factors? Where do I start?"
teach.praise: First take out anything common, then match a pattern like a² − b², and finally multiply back to check. x² − 49 = (x − 7)(x + 7)!
teach.nudge: Is 49 a square number? Which identity has a minus sign between two squares?

topics.title: Fraction squares, three-term squares and reciprocals

learn.hook: x + 1/x = 3? Then x² + 1/x² is exactly 7, and you never need to know x!
points: Perfect squares can have fractional coefficients: x² + x + 1/4 = (x + 1/2)² because 2 × x × 1/2 = x.
A six-term expression may be a three-term square: x² + 4y² + 9z² + 4xy + 12yz + 6zx = (x + 2y + 3z)². Find the square roots of the squared terms and check the cross terms.
(x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x², so x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2. Similarly x² + 1/x² = (x − 1/x)² + 2.
'A number plus its reciprocal is k' gives x + 1/x = k, which becomes the quadratic x² − kx + 1 = 0 after multiplying by x.

example.q: A number plus its reciprocal is 10/3. Find the number.

learn.reallife: Engineers simplify formulas with fractions by spotting perfect squares, just as you will here.

items.text: (a + b + c)² has ___ terms when expanded

quiz.q: Factorise x² + (2/3)x + 1/9.
quiz.mistake: Takes the square root of the middle coefficient

quiz.q: Expand (y/2 − 2)².
quiz.mistake: Halves the middle term twice

quiz.q: Which expression equals (a + 2b + c)²?
quiz.explain: Square each term and add twice each product: 2(a)(2b) = 4ab, 2(2b)(c) = 4bc, 2(c)(a) = 2ca.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to square the coefficient 2 in 2b

quiz.q: Factorise 4x² + y² + 9z² + 4xy + 6yz + 12zx.
quiz.explain: Square roots of the squares are 2x, y, 3z. Check: 2(2x)(y) = 4xy, 2(y)(3z) = 6yz, 2(3z)(2x) = 12zx.
quiz.mistake: Uses the squared coefficients instead of their square roots

quiz.q: If x + 1/x = 7, find x² + 1/x².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract 2, or adds it

quiz.q: If x − 1/x = 5, find x² + 1/x².
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 2 instead of adding

quiz.q: A number plus its reciprocal equals 5/2. Which numbers can it be?
quiz.mistake: Takes the given sum as the number

quiz.q: If a + b + c = 10 and a² + b² + c² = 38, find ab + bc + ca.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to halve

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "If x + 1/x = 3, how can I find x² + 1/x² without finding x?"
teach.praise: Clever! Square both sides and subtract 2 to get 7!
teach.nudge: What happens if you square x + 1/x? What extra number appears?

learn.hook: 11³ = 1331 and 101³ = 1030301. Patterns like these come straight from the cube identities!
points: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³.
(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b) = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³.
a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).
(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.
a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). So if a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
learn.reallife: Volumes of cube-shaped boxes grow as a cube. If each side of a 10 cm box grows by 1 cm, (a + b)³ shows exactly how much extra space you get.

games.title: Cube check
items: You also need the term 3ab(a + b). Try a = b = 1: 8 is not 2.
Multiply out the right side and the middle terms cancel, leaving a³ − b³.
If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc
This follows from a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(...), which is 0 when a + b + c = 0.
Use (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³ with a = x, b = 1.

quiz.q: Expand (x + 2)³.
quiz.explain: a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ with a = x, b = 2 gives x³ + 6x² + 12x + 8.
quiz.mistake: Cubes each term separately and drops the middle terms

quiz.q: Find 102³ using an identity.
quiz.mistake: Uses 3ab instead of 3ab(a + b), getting 1000608, or forgets the middle part entirely

quiz.q: Find (−12)³ + 7³ + 5³ without cubing each number.
quiz.explain: −12 + 7 + 5 = 0, so the sum of cubes equals 3abc = 3 × (−12) × 7 × 5 = −1260.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is 0 because a + b + c = 0, or drops the negative sign

quiz.q: Expand (x + y + 2)².
quiz.explain: Use a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca with c = 2: 2bc = 4y and 2ca = 4x.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the cross terms

quiz.q: Factorise x³ − 27.
quiz.explain: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) with a = x, b = 3.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the signs of the sum-of-cubes and difference-of-cubes identities

quiz.q: If x + y = 5 and xy = 6, find x³ + y³.
quiz.mistake: Thinks x³ + y³ = (x + y)³

quiz.q: Expand (2x − 1)³.
quiz.explain: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³ with a = 2x, b = 1: 8x³ − 12x² + 6x − 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to cube the 2 in 2x, or gets the alternating signs wrong

quiz.q: If a + b + c = 9 and ab + bc + ca = 26, find a² + b² + c².
quiz.explain: a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca) = 81 − 52 = 29.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 26 instead of 2 × 26

teach.ask: Gappu counts on his feathers: "Why does (a + b)³ have so many terms? Can't I just cube a and cube b?"
teach.praise: (a + b)³ is (a + b) multiplied three times, so the extra terms 3a²b + 3ab² appear. Just a³ + b³ is not enough!
teach.nudge: What do you get if you multiply (a + b)² by (a + b) once more?

topics.title: More cube identities and testing identities

learn.hook: Is (a + b)³ the same as a³ + b³? Try a = b = 1: 8 versus 2. One test is enough to bust a fake identity!
points: Sum of cubes: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx).
To use it with only x + y + z and xy + yz + zx known, first find x² + y² + z² = (x + y + z)² − 2(xy + yz + zx).
Verify an identity by multiplying out the right side and checking it equals the left side.
To test a claimed identity, try simple values. If even one value fails, it is NOT an identity; passing a few tests suggests (but does not prove) it is one.

example.q: If a + b + c = 15 and ab + bc + ca = 74, find a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc.

learn.reallife: Software testers do the same as you: one failing case proves a program (or an identity) is wrong.

games.title: Identity or not?
items: (a + b)² = a² + b² for all a, b

quiz.q: Factorise x³ + 125.
quiz.explain: Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) with b = 5.
quiz.mistake: Uses + ab in the second bracket, which belongs to a³ − b³

quiz.q: Use the sum of cubes to find 8³ + 2³ as (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
quiz.mistake: Cubes the sum: (8 + 2)³

quiz.q: Using x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx), find the value for x = 1, y = 2, z = 3.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the −3xyz term

quiz.q: If a + b + c = 12 and ab + bc + ca = 47, what is a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc?
quiz.mistake: Stops after finding the second bracket, or multiplies 12 by 47

quiz.q: Riya checks (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2 using a = 1, b = 1 and finds both sides equal 4. What can she conclude?
options: Nothing yet; she must test other values, and a = 2, b = 1 shows it fails
It is an identity for all whole numbers
quiz.explain: With a = 2, b = 1: 9 versus 4 + 1 + 2 = 7. One value that works does not prove an identity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one successful test proves an identity

quiz.q: Which value shows that (x + 1)² = x² + 1 is not an identity?
quiz.explain: x = 1: left 4, right 2. (x = 0 gives 1 = 1, which hides the error.)
quiz.mistake: Tests only x = 0

quiz.q: To verify a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), you multiply out the right side. Which terms cancel?
quiz.explain: (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) = a³ + a²b + ab² − a²b − ab² − b³ = a³ − b³.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the cubes cancel

quiz.q: If a + b + c = 6 and ab + bc + ca = 11, find a² + b² + c².
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the pairwise sum

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I know if something is really an identity?"
teach.praise: Great thinking! It must work for every value; one failure busts it!
teach.nudge: Does an identity work for some values or all values? What does one failing value tell you?

learn.hook: Factorising can be done with your hands: arrange tiles into a perfect rectangle and read off the sides!
points: Algebra tiles: a big square of side x has area x², a long strip x by 1 has area x, and a small unit square has area 1.
To factor x² + 7x + 12, take 1 big square, 7 strips and 12 unit squares, and arrange them into a rectangle.
The rectangle's sides are the factors: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4). The units form a 3 × 4 block and the strips split 3 and 4.
A path around a square ground of side x and width w covers (x + 2w)² − x² = 4wx + 4w²; tiles show the four strips and four corner squares.

steps: Units arranged 2 × 3; strips 2 on one side, 3 on the other

learn.reallife: A gardener laying a paved border around a square lawn can count the paving stones the same way.

games.title: Build x² + 6x + 8
items: Find two numbers with product 8 and sum 6: 2 and 4
Put 2 strips on one side and 4 on the other
Fill the corner with 2 × 4 = 8 unit squares

quiz.q: Which tile has area x?
options: A strip of length x and width 1
A strip of length 1 and width 1/x
quiz.mistake: Confuses the strip with the big square

quiz.q: How many unit squares are needed to show x² + 9x + 14?
quiz.explain: The constant term 14 is the number of unit tiles.
quiz.mistake: Uses the coefficient of x

quiz.q: Tiles for x² + 9x + 14 make a rectangle. What are its sides?
quiz.mistake: Uses the coefficients directly as the sides

quiz.q: Rohan arranges 1 x²-tile, 6 strips and 9 units into a square. What is its side?
quiz.explain: x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)², so the rectangle is a square.
quiz.mistake: Takes the number of strips as the side

quiz.q: With 1 x²-tile, 5 strips and 4 units, which rectangle is possible?
quiz.mistake: Ignores the number of strips

quiz.q: A square park of side x m has a path 2 m wide all around it on the outside. What is the area of the path?
quiz.mistake: Adds the width only once on each side

quiz.q: For the same path with x = 20, what is the path's area?
quiz.mistake: Gives the park's area instead of the path's

quiz.q: Why can x² + 3x + 5 not be made into a rectangle with whole tiles?
options: No two whole numbers have product 5 and sum 3
quiz.mistake: Thinks any set of tiles forms a rectangle

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How can tiles help me factor x² + 7x + 12?"
teach.praise: Brilliant! Arrange the tiles into a rectangle and its sides are the factors!
teach.nudge: What shape do you make with the tiles? How do you read off the factors?

learn.hook: 6x² + 7x − 3 looks scary, but find two numbers that multiply to −18 and add to 7, and it falls apart!
points: For ax² + bx + c, find two numbers with product a × c and sum b. Split bx using them, then group in pairs.
Example: 6x² + 7x − 3; a × c = −18, the numbers are 9 and −2: 6x² + 9x − 2x − 3 = 3x(2x + 3) − 1(2x + 3) = (3x − 1)(2x + 3).
For x² + px + q (a = 1) just find two numbers with product q and sum p: r² − r − 42 = (r − 7)(r + 6).
If (x − k) is a factor of a polynomial, then putting x = k makes it zero; this links its coefficients.
n³ − n = (n − 1)n(n + 1), a product of three consecutive integers, so it is always divisible by 2 and by 3, hence by 6.

steps: a × c = 6; numbers 6 and 1 add to 7

learn.reallife: Splitting things smartly into pairs is how quiz teams split prize money and how this method splits the middle term.

quiz.q: Factorise y² − 11y + 28.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the sign of the middle term

quiz.q: Factorise 3x² + 10x + 8.
quiz.mistake: Checks the product but not the middle term

quiz.q: Factorise 6x² − x − 2.
quiz.mistake: Gets the signs of the factors swapped

quiz.q: To factor 4x² + 4x − 15, which two numbers should split 4x?
quiz.mistake: Uses the product c only, not a × c
Picks the number that matches the middle coefficient

quiz.q: (x − 2) and (x − 1/2) are both factors of px² + 5x + r. Substituting x = 2 and x = 1/2 gives 4p + 10 + r = 0 and p + 10 + 4r = 0. What follows?
quiz.explain: Subtract the second from the first: 3p − 3r = 0.
quiz.mistake: Adds the equations instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Using p = r in 4p + 10 + r = 0, what is p?
quiz.mistake: Drops the sign

quiz.q: Why is n³ − n always divisible by 6 for whole numbers n?
options: It equals (n − 1)n(n + 1), three consecutive numbers, so it has a factor 2 and a factor 3
quiz.explain: Among three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even.
quiz.mistake: Checks one example and calls it proof

teach.praise: Yes! Two numbers with product a × c and sum b, then split and group!
teach.nudge: Which two numbers do you look for? What do they multiply to and add to?

learn.hook: Just as 12/18 cancels to 2/3, (x² − 9)/(x + 3) cancels to x − 3 — but watch out for x = −3!
points: A rational expression is a ratio of two polynomials, P(x)/Q(x), with Q(x) not the zero polynomial.
To simplify, factorise the numerator and the denominator fully, then cancel common factors (whole factors only, never single terms).
Values that make the denominator zero are not allowed. List them from the original denominator, before cancelling.
learn.reallife: Scientists simplify formulas before plugging in numbers, but they always note the values where the formula breaks down.

quiz.q: Which of these is a rational expression?
quiz.explain: It is a ratio of two polynomials.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any expression with a fraction bar or root qualifies

quiz.q: Simplify (x² − 25)/(x + 5).
quiz.mistake: Cancels single terms instead of factors

quiz.q: Simplify (x² + 7x + 10)/(x² + 3x − 10).
quiz.mistake: Cancels the x² terms

quiz.q: For which values is (x + 1)/(x² − 4) not defined?
quiz.mistake: Looks for zeros of the numerator

quiz.q: Simplify (3x² − 6x)/(6x).
quiz.mistake: Cancels 3 but not the x

quiz.q: Riya simplifies (x + 4)/4 to x. What went wrong?
options: She cancelled a single term, not a common factor
quiz.explain: 4 is not a factor of the whole numerator x + 4, so it cannot be cancelled.
quiz.mistake: Cancels terms joined by + signs

quiz.q: (x² − 9)/(x − 3) simplifies to x + 3. What is the value of the simplified form at x = 5?
quiz.mistake: Substitutes into the wrong expression

quiz.q: After simplifying (x² − 9)/(x − 3) to x + 3, is x = 3 allowed?
options: Yes, all values are allowed after cancelling
No, the original denominator is 0 at x = 3
quiz.explain: Restrictions come from the original expression, before cancelling.
quiz.mistake: Takes restrictions from the simplified form only

teach.ask: Gappu asks: "How do I simplify (x² − 9)/(x + 3)? Can I put any x in?"
teach.praise: Excellent! Factorise, cancel common factors, and exclude values that make the denominator zero!
teach.nudge: What do you do before cancelling? Which x-values must you exclude?
